Critical lab results must reach the ordering clinician within 60 minutes [1].

If you can't reach the ordering clinician within 30 minutes, the result goes to the medical director on call [1]. Every critical result notification is documented in the chart with the time and the person notified [1].

To reach the on-call medical director, call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. The service pages the on-call medical director and, if there's no callback within 10 minutes, pages the backup. Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers, because pages through the answering service are logged and timed, which the chart documentation needs [2].

Note that the escalation protocol's "urgent same-day" section sets a different 30-minute window for a critical lab value called in by the reference lab: notify the supervising physician within 30 minutes [1]. That is a separate step from the 60-minute ordering-clinician rule, so the 30-minute supervising-physician notification applies to reference-lab calls, and the 60-minute deadline still governs the ordering clinician.

Emergency access to a customer workspace lasts **2 hours**. It needs approval from a second engineer, not from a manager or the Head of Security [1].

**Duration:** The access expires after 2 hours. That is deliberately shorter than the standard 8-hour Teleport production session [1][2]. If you need more time, you have to submit a new request with an update on the case [1].

**Approval:**
- Request it with `nwctl access request --workspace <id> --reason <case-or-incident-id>` [1].
- A second engineer from the support or on-call rotation must approve it in Teleport [1].
- You cannot approve your own request, and the approver must not be on the same case [1].

**Conditions:**
- It is only allowed when there is an open support case or a declared incident. Every request must reference that case or incident ID [1].
- Access is read-only by default. Write access, such as editing a pipeline on the customer's behalf, needs the customer's written consent recorded in the case first [1].
- All sessions are recorded [2].

No. Public chatbots and general-purpose AI assistants are not approved for Halcyon staff on any device, and removing the name doesn't change that. The AI policy says "de-identified" is not a loophole, because removing a name is not enough to make a case non-identifiable, so treat any patient details as PHI [1].

Only two AI tools on the approved list may handle PHI, and neither is a general chatbot:
- **Quillon Ambient** is an AI scribe for pilot clinics (Riverside and Elm Park) that drafts visit notes with patient verbal consent [1][4].
- **Meridian draft replies** drafts patient portal responses inside Meridian EHR, and a clinician must edit or approve them before they are sent [1].

Halcyon Assist is approved only for policy questions, and you must not paste patient details into it, even without names [1].

If you've already pasted patient information into a chatbot, report it to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours by emailing privacy@halcyon.example or calling the compliance hotline [3].

rows.answer:
**17 lab results** were filed into the wrong patient's chart in the Bayline incident (July 21–23, 2026, at the Riverside and Northgate clinics) [1].

**Why it happened:** The root cause analysis found three system-level causes [1]:

- **Unannounced feed change:** On July 20, Bayline changed its results feed and moved the medical record number (MRN) into a different HL7 segment, without notice [1].
- **Weak fallback matching:** When the MRN was missing, the Switchyard interface engine matched results on last name and year of birth only. That rule had existed since 2021 and had never been used at volume [1].
- **No monitoring or change-notice requirement:** Nobody was alerted that 100% of Bayline results were using the fallback rule, and the Bayline agreement did not require advance notice of format changes [1].

The error was caught on July 23 when a medical assistant at Riverside noticed a potassium result that didn't match the patient's history. The feed was stopped, and the MRN mapping was corrected before the feed was restored on July 24 [1]. Two patients had abnormal results go to another chart, with follow-up delayed by four and six days. The RCA says neither suffered lasting harm [1].

A related fix is tracked as project Heron, a positive patient identification check before lab results are released to the patient portal (RCA-26-07, action 4). Its status is "build complete; awaiting release," with a Q4 2026 target [3].

At Halcyon, the equivalent is a **root cause analysis (RCA)**, which must be completed within **45 calendar days** of the event becoming known, not five business days [4]. The policy applies RCAs to every Level 1 and Level 2 event, so a serious patient safety event falls under it [4].

Related deadlines in the same policy:
- **Within 1 hour:** for a sentinel event, the charge nurse notifies the on-call medical director [4].
- **Within 72 hours:** QPS charters the RCA team [4].
- **Reporting:** anyone involved or who witnessed the event files a report in SafeReport, and this is never optional [4].

The policy doesn't set a separate deadline for the Patient Safety Committee review. It says the committee meets monthly and reviews completed RCAs with their action plans [4].

The knowledge base doesn't use the term "incident commander" for Halcyon clinics. The closest equivalent is the **charge nurse**, who coordinates the immediate response to any patient safety event, as described in the sentinel and adverse event reporting policy [1].

Who fills that role depends on the clinic's size and shift:

- **Large clinics:** the staffing standard requires two RNs on site, with one designated charge nurse [1].
- **Medium and small clinics:** a charge nurse is designated whenever two or more RNs are on shift. Otherwise, the clinic manager fills the role [1].
- **No charge nurse on shift:** the clinic manager is the escalation point for the site [3].

The charge nurse also notifies the on-call medical director of sentinel events [2]. For a medical emergency, the clinical escalation protocol says to call 911 and notify the on-site clinician immediately [4].

Before Halcyon shares patient data with a vendor, it needs a signed business associate agreement (BAA) and a completed security risk assessment. Halcyon's documents use "BAA" rather than "DPA."

**Required before any PHI is shared**

- **Signed BAA.** Under the HIPAA privacy policy, a vendor that will create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on Halcyon's behalf is a business associate, and a signed BAA must be in place before any PHI is disclosed. This includes test files or "just a few names" for a pilot [6].
- **Security risk assessment.** Any tool or system that will handle PHI needs one [7][8].
- **Inventory entry.** The system must be listed in the clinical and business systems inventory before go-live [7][8].
- **Clinical safety review (clinical use only).** For clinical tools, the CMIO must complete a clinical safety review [7].

Only approved systems may hold PHI. Staff must not put PHI into unapproved AI tools [7][10].

**Current status example:** Tallgrass Survey Co. has a completed security risk assessment (September 2026, passed with conditions), but its BAA is not executed. Halcyon's rule is that no PHI may be shared with Tallgrass until the BAA is signed [6].

Northwind has a close equivalent, but it covers a different situation. Halcyon's break-the-glass is for clinicians opening a patient chart outside their normal care relationship. Northwind's emergency access is for its support and on-call engineers reaching into a customer's workspace during a case or incident.

**Halcyon (Meridian EHR)**
- Used when a patient needs care and you're outside your normal panel, such as an unscheduled walk-in or covering for a colleague [1].
- You click "Emergency access," pick a reason (Emergency care, Coverage, or Other), and type a justification. Access lasts up to 12 hours [1].
- No one approves it in the moment. The event is logged and reviewed by the Privacy Officer's team within 2 business days, and a manager is asked to confirm unclear reasons [1].
- Misuse is a privacy incident and can lead to sanctions up to termination [1].

**Northwind (customer workspaces)**
- Used only when there is an open support case or declared incident. Each request must reference that case or incident ID [2].
- A second engineer from the support or on-call rotation must approve it in Teleport. You can't approve your own request, and the approver can't be on the same case [2].
- Access is read-only by default. Write access needs the customer's written consent in the case first [2].
- It expires after 2 hours, much shorter than the standard 8-hour Teleport production session [2].
- Every session is recorded and kept for one year. The customer's audit log shows the access, and enterprise admins are emailed within 24 hours. Security reviews a sample of sessions weekly, plus every session that used write access [2].

**Key differences**
- **Approval:** Halcyon has none at the time of access and reviews afterward. Northwind requires a second engineer to approve beforehand.
- **Duration:** Halcyon allows up to 12 hours. Northwind allows 2 hours, with renewal requiring a case update.
- **Default permissions:** Halcyon's access is effectively full chart access. Northwind's is read-only unless the customer consents to write access.
- **Justification:** Halcyon requires a free-text reason. Northwind requires a case or incident ID.
- **Customer visibility:** Northwind notifies the customer's admins. Halcyon's documents don't describe any patient notification.
- **Review:** Halcyon's review is by the Privacy Officer's team within 2 business days. Northwind's is a weekly sample by Security.

Northwind's policy is in its information security policy and its emergency access guide [2][3]. The Halcyon rules are in its break-the-glass policy [1].

No, not for the sensitive data that matters most, at either company. Halcyon's rule is absolute. Northwind's is narrower.

**Halcyon Health:** Never. Slack is on the list of systems that must not hold PHI, with the note "Never, including DMs" [2]. The HIPAA policy says PHI may only be stored in the EHR, the practice management system, and approved systems, and never in Slack [3]. Use the EHR's secure messaging for patient communication, and `[secure]` encrypted email for outside providers [3].

**Northwind Labs:** Restricted data is never allowed in Slack. Customer event payloads, credentials and encryption keys must never leave production, and never go in tickets or Slack [1]. Support staff are told to use field names and counts instead of pasting payloads [4]. Confidential data (financials, contracts, employee data) is shared on a need-to-know basis [1]. The policy doesn't explicitly ban Slack for that tier, so check with the data owner before posting it there.

Reporting is different: Northwind asks people to report suspected incidents in `#security-help` [1]. Report the problem there, but without the sensitive payload itself.

You need two sign-offs, and the Head of Security sign-off is the one people tend to miss.

1. **Change approver of PLAT (Platform): Oluwaseun Adeyemi.** Delegate: Kofi Mensah [9]. Archived customer events are stored in Driftwood, which PLAT owns [6]. Changes to lifecycle rules, retention settings, or anything that deletes customer data on a schedule are "normal changes" that need this approver's sign-off [3].

2. **Head of Security: Tomasz Wierzbicki**, or the Security on-call delegate [3][9]. Driftwood is classed as Restricted [6], and normal changes to a Restricted service also need security sign-off [3].

**Other requirements for this change:**
- Label the PR `change:normal`, fill in the risk and rollback sections, and request review from the approver (or delegate) as a CODEOWNERS reviewer. For Restricted services, also request `@northwind/security` [3].
- Approvals are valid for 7 days. If the change hasn't shipped by then, re-request [3].
- Any change that alters how long customer data is kept also needs an ADR, linked from the PR [3].
- If the change shortens retention and an Enterprise contract references a retention period, the account team must give 30 days' customer notice [3].
- Check the freeze windows. The holiday freeze runs December 18, 2026 to January 4, 2027, and there is a month-end billing freeze on Ledger only [3].

The current default for archived event payloads in Driftwood is 365 days under the v2 retention standard [2]. Note that Security owns the retention standard itself [1][2], so if the change alters the standard rather than just the lifecycle rule, check with Security as well.

Changing reminder times is a significant change, so it needs three approvals. The reminders run on Pillbox, which is owned by Digital Health Engineering — Patient Engagement (DHE-PE) [5].

1. **System steward:** Felix Brandt, for DHE-PE [1].
2. **Clinical safety sign-off:** the CMIO, Dr. Anjali Rao, or her delegate, Associate CMIO Dr. Benedict Osei [1].
3. **CSCAB review:** the weekly Clinical Systems Change Advisory Board, which meets Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern [1].

Patient-facing automation such as reminders counts as a significant change [1]. Since the IR-0412 incident, reminders also carry an idempotency key so the same dose isn't sent twice [4]. If your change also moves the scheduler to a different runner or server, it needs a written runbook that states how double-running is prevented [1].

The fix would need three approvals, because changing how results are routed is a significant change under the clinical systems change control policy:

1. **System steward: Owen Mbeki, Integration Services (INT).** The steward approves changes to the team's systems [2]. Bayline's HL7 results feed into Switchyard is owned by INT [5], and Switchyard's fallback matching caused the misfiling [1].
2. **Clinical safety sign-off: Dr. Anjali Rao, CMIO**, or her delegate, Associate CMIO Dr. Benedict Osei [2].
3. **Review at the Clinical Systems Change Advisory Board (CSCAB)**, which meets Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern [2].

An emergency change, meaning one that stops ongoing patient harm, can be approved by the on-call medical director, with CSCAB reviewing it at its next meeting [2]. Cutovers also need a written runbook that explains how double-running is prevented [2].

The feed was already restored on July 24 with the MRN mapping corrected [1]. The root cause analysis also lists a fallback-matching weakness and no monitoring of fallback-matched messages as causes [1], so the fix may need the same approvals.

The three big bets picked at the cycle 5 pitch review were:

1. **Tributary**, streaming joins (the Enrich step), pitched by Mateo and LZ [1]. The pitch scope was CDC-backed snapshots, the editor preview, dead-letter routing for unmatched events, and a private beta with design partners in October, with GA targeted for January 2027 [1].

3. **Hydrant**, automatic per-cell scaling for ingest gateways, pitched by OA [1]. It also carried the gateway TLS session ticket change from INC-2291 as a small batch item [1].

Several of these have moved since the pitch review:

- **Tributary:** The private beta started October 1 with eight design partners, and GA stays January 2027. Security sign-off on persisted snapshots is still outstanding and is the main risk [6].
- **Lantern:** GA has slipped from January to March 2027, and the beta has moved from December to February [6]. The October codename register also lists beta in February 2027 and GA in March 2027 [4].
- **Hydrant:** It shipped to all production cells on October 22, 2026 [3][4].

rows.answer:
When a customer goes over their limit, the API returns **HTTP 429**, and the response includes a **`Retry-After` header** giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying [1].

**What the customer gets back**
- Status: HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) [1].
- Header: `Retry-After`, the number of seconds to wait [1].
- Rejected requests don't count against the monthly event quota [1].

**How they know when to retry**
- They read the `Retry-After` value and wait that long. Northwind's SDKs honour this header automatically and also back off exponentially [1].
- Customers using their own HTTP client need to implement this themselves. The source doesn't describe a separate reset-time header or a documented error body.

**Useful context on the limits**
- Limits apply per workspace, not per API key, so all keys in one workspace share one budget [1].
- Short bursts up to 2x the limit are allowed for 10 seconds [1].
- Limits vary by endpoint and plan. For example, `POST /v2/events` is 100 req/s on Starter, 2,000 req/s on Growth, and 10,000 req/s on Enterprise by default [1].
- Endpoints not included in a customer's plan return HTTP 403, not 429 [1].

The rate-limit page is the internal source of truth, and the public docs copy it on each release [1].

Five production services are classed as Restricted [1]:

- **Conduit**: source and destination connectors. Stores encrypted connector credentials and sync cursors. Owner: DP [1].
- **Driftwood**: long-term object archive behind the hot buffer. Stores archived event payloads, partitioned by workspace and day. Owner: PLAT [1].
- **ingest-gateway**: accepts events from customer SDKs and the HTTP API. Stores in-flight event payloads only, with nothing persisted beyond the Kafka hot buffer. Owner: DP [1].
- **Keystone**: authentication and authorization. Stores hashed API keys, SSO/SAML configuration, and session tokens. Owner: IDB [1].
- **runner**: executes customer pipelines. Stores partition state in local RocksDB and reference-table snapshots. Owner: DP [1].

A 22% discount on an Enterprise first-year contract needs approval from the **Regional sales director**. The quote also goes through the deal desk first, because any discount above 15% is routed there automatically [1].

- **Approval level:** Over 15% up to 25% on Enterprise deals is the Regional sales director, with a target turnaround of 1 business day [1].
- **Deal desk:** Discounts above 15% are reviewed by the deal desk, which is run by Priscilla Okoye in sales operations. It checks margin, payment terms and non-standard clauses before forwarding to the approver [1].
- **Recording:** The approver must record the decision in the CRM. Email and Slack approvals do not count [1].
- **Validity:** Approvals last 30 days. If the quote changes by more than 2 percentage points, it needs fresh approval [1].

The older Pricing and discount policy says a 20–30% discount needs VP of Sales approval [2]. The Sales desk memo replaces that table from October 1, 2026, so the regional director applies now [1]. The 22% is measured against first-year contract value at list price [1][2].

Your deploy bakes in the canary cell for **45 minutes** before it can be promoted automatically. The October 2026 pipeline change raised this from 20 minutes because some failures only appear after caches or sessions expire, and INC-2291 showed 20 minutes was too short to catch them [1].

The engineering handbook still says 20 minutes [2]. The October note says that where the two differ, the note applies and the handbook will be updated to match [1], so 45 minutes is the current rule.

Promotion also now requires:
- Error rate and p95 latency within 10% of baseline (unchanged) [1].
- Zero sustained TLS handshake errors between gateways and brokers in canary [1].
- Runner consumer lag growing by no more than 2 minutes during the bake [1].

Anyone can run `/deploy hold <deploy-id>` in Slack to keep a deploy in canary while they check something [1].

rows.answer:
**No, don't run `nwctl scale ingest` by hand.** The runbook step is out of date. Hydrant, the autoscaler, has replaced it in us-west, and Hydrant will revert a manual change within 2 minutes [2].

- **Hydrant should already be scaling us-west.** It went live in us-west on October 15 [2]. It scales up when average gateway CPU stays above 65% for 3 minutes, adding 25% of current replicas (at least 2) per step [2]. With CPU above 80%, it should be acting on its own.
- **Check the ceiling.** us-west's Hydrant floor and ceiling are 10 and 48 replicas [3]. If the cell sits at its ceiling for 10 minutes, Hydrant pages the Data Plane primary on-call, since that usually points to a gateway problem rather than real traffic [2].
- **If you need to pin the count** (for example, while debugging a bad gateway build), use a hold: `nwctl hydrant hold --cell us-west --replicas <n> --ttl 2h`. Holds can last at most 4 hours and need no approval. Release early with `nwctl hydrant release --cell us-west` [2].
- **Still follow the rest of the 5xx steps.** Check which cell is affected and look at gateway TLS handshake errors first [1][2]. The INC-2291 outage in us-east came from a certificate bundle missing the intermediate CA, which caused TLS handshake failures across all gateways in the cell [5].

If the 5xx rate keeps climbing even though Hydrant is scaling, or if it's stuck at the ceiling, escalate to the Data Plane primary on-call. For a SEV-1 or SEV-2, declare the incident with `/incident declare` in Slack [1].

Archived events stay in the attic for **365 days** by default. The attic is Driftwood, the long-term event archive [3], and the current retention standard (v2, effective September 15, 2026) sets archived event payloads in Driftwood at 365 days [2]. That replaced the earlier default of 400 days in v1 [1][2].

Lifecycle rules on the Driftwood buckets delete objects once they pass their retention period, and per-workspace overrides are stored as bucket tags [2]. Enterprise customers can contract for longer archive retention, up to 730 days, with security team approval [2].

rows.answer:
An Enterprise workspace can force a reference-table snapshot rebuild **once every 2 minutes** through `POST /v2/reference-tables/{id}/refresh` [1]. This is the default Enterprise limit in the rate-limit table [1].

The source also says these refreshes are deliberately limited. A forced refresh discards the runner's snapshot and rebuilds it with a full table scan, which is expensive for large tables, and the limits "will not be raised for anyone" [1]. The Enterprise contract-raise option described in the same document covers ingest endpoints (`/v2/events` and `/v2/events/batch`), not this refresh endpoint [1].

rows.answer:
No, don't throw them out. The formulary's cold-chain procedure says not to discard anything when a refrigerator reads outside 2–8 °C [1].

1. **Label the affected stock "Do not use."** Keep it refrigerated in a working unit, and record the reading, the time and how long it has been out of range [1].
2. **Call the clinical pharmacist within 1 hour.** The pharmacist checks with the manufacturers whether the stock can still be used [1].
3. **File a SafeReport.** It is a Level 4 near miss if no vaccine was given. It is higher if a patient received vaccine from the affected stock [1].
4. **Give no vaccine from that stock** until the clinical pharmacist releases it in writing [1].

Frozen vaccines are never refrozen or reused once thawed [1].

- **Sensitive records:** Records with extra legal protection, such as substance use treatment records, are released only after the Privacy Officer reviews the request [1].

Nothing is charged. Halcyon eliminated the no-show fee under the policy revised in October 2026, which took effect October 5, 2026 [1]. Today is October 31, 2026, so that policy applies.

- **Current policy:** A missed appointment counts as a no-show only if the patient did not cancel at least 2 hours ahead. Halcyon no longer charges patients for missed appointments [1]. Patients are not discharged for no-shows [1].
- **Old fees:** Any no-show fees billed before October 5, 2026 that are still unpaid are waived. Revenue Cycle Management reverses them on statements, and front desk staff should not try to collect them [1].
- **Superseded rule:** The 2025 policy charged a $25 fee for each no-show after the second in a 12-month period, and it exempted Medicaid and sliding-fee patients [2]. That policy was replaced in full [1], so it no longer applies.

For a third no-show in 12 months, a care coordinator calls the patient to offer help such as ride vouchers or a telehealth visit [1].

A patient who arrives **more than 10 minutes** after their appointment time is offered the next open slot that day with any clinician, or rescheduled. This is the current rule under the policy revised October 5, 2026 [1]. The clinician may still see the patient if the schedule allows [1].

The earlier March 2025 policy used a **15-minute** threshold [2]. The 2026 revision replaced it, so the 10-minute rule applies now.

Patients who are late because of an interpreter or accessibility issue on Halcyon's side are never rescheduled for being late [1][2].

The 2025 standard set this at 1.5 for large clinics (over 90 visits a day), and it has been replaced [1][2].

Related minimums for a large clinic under the current standard: 3 physicians or NPs on site, 2 RNs on site (one designated as charge nurse), and 4 front desk staff [2].

No. Since September 1, 2026, a small clinic must have at least one RN on site during open hours. The 2026 standard replaced the 2025 version, which did not require an RN in small clinics [2]. The minimum is one physician or NP, one RN, one MA per clinician, and two front desk staff [2].

Under the 2026 bands, a small clinic averages under 40 visits a day [2]. Using the July–September 2026 averages, the small sites are Elmhurst (38) and Cedar Hollow (31) [4]. Riverbend (46) falls in the medium band [2][4]. Bands are reset each quarter, so this can change [4].

If coverage drops, the clinic manager contacts the float pool first, and only then converts in-person visits to telehealth where clinically appropriate [2]. The float pool keeps 2 RNs on call daily [2]. The documents I have don't say what to do specifically when an RN is missing, so check with Clinical Operations before running a day without one.

The Meridian EHR upgrade cutover is planned for **Saturday, February 6, 2027, starting at 22:00 Eastern**, with **6 hours of planned downtime** [3]. That means the system is expected to be down until about 04:00 Sunday, February 7. The CSCAB approved the plan, and the final go/no-go is at CSCAB on January 27, 2027 [3].

Clinics will use paper downtime procedures during the window. The cutover must finish by 04:00 Sunday so that verification is done before Harbor Point's Sunday clinic opens at 10:00 [3].

The upgrade is project "Wren" (release 2027.1), which is in integrated testing with a Q1 2027 target [2]. Meridian Clinical Systems will staff a live bridge line with its own engineers for the whole cutover window [4].

The same CSCAB minutes also record a separate decision to release something on November 18, 2026 [3]. The excerpt doesn't say what that release is, so I can't confirm whether it relates to the Meridian upgrade.

It is maintained by the **Platform team** (last updated October 2, 2026) [1]. The catalog's stated purpose is to be the source of truth for "which production service does what, what data it keeps, and which team owns it," and it says owning teams are listed by short code, with the engineering team directory showing who is behind each code [1].

Key differences from your inventory:

- **Scope:** Northwind's catalog covers software services, not PHI. It classifies data as Restricted, Confidential, or Internal instead [1]. Northwind's Production services list has 9 services: 5 Restricted, 2 Confidential, and 2 Internal [1].
- **Owners:** Owners are team codes such as DP, PLAT, IDB, WX, and OBS. Examples: Keystone (Restricted) is owned by IDB, and Atlas (Confidential) by WX [1].
- **Shared infrastructure:** A separate list covers Kafka, Kubernetes, managed Postgres, and Teleport. Owners are PLAT for three components and SEC for Teleport [1].

rows.answer:
Patient safety events at Halcyon are reported in **SafeReport**, and anyone involved or who witnessed the event files the report. The policy's "Within 24 hours" section sets out the steps [1].

**Who files:** Anyone involved in or who witnessed the event. Reporting is never optional and never punished [1].

**How soon:**
- **Immediately:** Make the patient safe and follow the clinical escalation protocol, calling 911 if needed [1][5].
- **Right away:** Tell the charge nurse on shift. If the clinic has no charge nurse on shift, tell the clinic manager [1].
- **Within 1 hour (sentinel events only):** The charge nurse notifies the on-call medical director [1]. Sentinel events include patient death or permanent harm unrelated to the natural course of illness, wrong-patient or wrong-site procedures, and patient suicide within 72 hours of a visit [1][2].
- **Within 24 hours:** The filing steps above are listed under this heading. I did not find a separate, explicit filing deadline in the sources.

**After filing:** Every Level 1 and Level 2 event gets a root cause analysis. QPS charters the team within 72 hours, and the RCA must be completed within 45 calendar days of the event becoming known [1]. Completed RCAs go to the Patient Safety Committee, chaired by Dr. Kenji Watanabe [1].

**Other routes:**
- **Privacy incidents** (such as a misdirected fax or lost device) are separate. Report them to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours at privacy@halcyon.example or via the compliance hotline [6].
- **Out-of-hours escalation:** Call the answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2 to page the on-call medical director [4].

I did not find the Northwind `/incident declare` process in the knowledge base, so I can't compare it with the Halcyon steps.

Northwind uses a similar approach, though it calls it "blameless" rather than "just culture." Every SEV-1 and SEV-2 gets a blameless postmortem within five business days of resolution. The postmortem looks at the system and process, not individuals, and names appear only in the timeline [3]. Postmortems are reviewed at the Thursday reliability meeting [2].

Who writes it: the incident commander picks the author, usually the responder who knew the most about the failure [3]. Examples from the record:
- INC-2291 (SEV-1, August 14): postmortem author Priya Raman, with the ingest team [4].
- INC-2340 (SEV-2, October 6): the IC, Kofi Mensah, named Arjun Mehta as postmortem owner, due October 13 [6].

Note that the knowledge base doesn't say whether Northwind's postmortems have a separate facilitator or a formal just-culture review step beyond the Thursday meeting. Its incident log also shows INC-2351's postmortem draft is due for review on November 5 [1].

**Short answer:** Northwind does run periodic access reviews, and unconfirmed access is revoked automatically. But the EHR your compliance team reviews is Halcyon's Meridian EHR, and I found no equivalent recertification step in Halcyon's documents.

**Northwind (its own systems and customer data):** Its information security policy says quarterly access reviews are run by each team lead, and access that is not re-confirmed is revoked automatically [3]. Production access is granted through Teleport and expires after 8 hours, and standing access to production databases is not allowed for anyone [3].

**Halcyon (Meridian EHR):** Halcyon's documents describe a different control. The compliance team reviews EHR access logs monthly using automated anomaly detection, and unusual access triggers a review with the employee's manager [1]. I did not find a documented quarterly or periodic manager sign-off on continued EHR access, or a stated consequence if no one signs off. The closest rules are:
- Access to clinical systems is suspended automatically if HIPAA training is more than 14 days overdue [1].
- Every break-the-glass event is reviewed by the Privacy Officer's team within 2 business days, and the manager is asked to confirm the reason if it's unclear [2].

If your compliance team expects a periodic access attestation for Meridian, it may be defined in a document I couldn't find. I'd check with the Privacy Officer (Margaret Holloway) or the HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui) to confirm.

rows.answer:
**Short answer:** Halcyon's requirements apply to a tool that touches patient data (PHI). The usual turnaround is 6–10 weeks, mostly waiting on the business associate agreement. The knowledge base does not give a timeline for Northwind's `#vendor-review` process.

**What Halcyon requires before staff use an AI tool with PHI**

Staff email the Privacy Officer (Margaret Holloway) and the HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui). Any tool that will handle PHI needs:
1. A security risk assessment.
2. A signed business associate agreement with the vendor.
3. An entry in the clinical and business systems inventory.
4. For clinical use, a clinical safety review by the CMIO [1].

PHI may not go into any AI tool that isn't on Halcyon's approved list [1][2]. "De-identified" doesn't count as a workaround, so treat any patient details as PHI [1].

**How long it takes**

Halcyon's stated typical turnaround is 6–10 weeks, mostly waiting on the BAA [1]. The Quillon Ambient scribe is an example: its BAA was executed July 30, 2026, and its security risk assessment was completed in July 2026 [3].

**Northwind's side**

Any software that will process customer data must go through the security review in `#vendor-review` before it's used [4]. The knowledge base doesn't say how long that review takes or what it requires. Northwind's vendor register does show the kinds of items it tracks, including a signed DPA, SOC 2 status, data residency, and the review outcome [5][6].

Halcyon's equivalent is the **system steward for the Digital Health Engineering — Patient Engagement team (DHE-PE), Felix Brandt**. The Halcyon app, which includes bill pay, is owned by DHE-PE [1][4].

A purely cosmetic change is a **minor change** under Halcyon's policy, which requires **steward approval only** [1]. So his OK is enough on its own, as long as the change stays cosmetic.

Two caveats:
- **Scope matters.** Anything that touches patient-facing automation, the app's clinical content, medication information, or results routing is a significant change. That requires the steward, clinical safety sign-off from the CMIO (Dr. Anjali Rao) or her delegate (Dr. Benedict Osei), and review at the weekly CSCAB meeting [1]. If your tweak changes wording that patients act on, or anything beyond appearance, treat it as significant.
- **Bill pay holds PHI.** The Halcyon app holds intake forms and insurance card images [4]. The policy doesn't say a cosmetic change needs a privacy review, but it's worth confirming with the HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui) if the change touches data handling.

rows.answer:
**Northwind Labs (October duplicate invoices, INC-2340):** The main fix is an idempotency key on invoice creation, scoped to each workspace and billing period. The root cause was that the payment provider's webhook timed out during the first batch, the retry re-ran the batch, and invoice creation wasn't idempotent [8]. The key shipped October 8 and is marked Done [10]. Engineering also ran a dry run after the deploy and got zero duplicates [8]. Two related follow-ups exist:
- A daily reconciliation report comparing invoices to charges is Done [10].
- An alert for when the provider webhook times out during a billing batch is still Open, due November 6 [10].

**Halcyon Health (September duplicate medication reminders, IR-0412):** The fix is an idempotency key on each reminder, made from patient, medication and scheduled time. A reminder with an existing key is never sent again [1]. The incident happened because a September 2 scheduler change ran the old and new job runners at the same time, and neither checked whether a reminder had already gone out [1]. To prevent a repeat, Halcyon also requires that scheduler cutovers come with a written runbook stating how double-running is prevented, plus clinical safety sign-off [1][2]. The reminder wording change ("If you already took this dose, you don't need to take it again") is a patient-facing mitigation, not a technical control [1].

One discrepancy: the Slack export says the Northwind fix was merged and deployed on October 6 [8], while the status sheet says it shipped October 8 [10].

**Northwind Labs has a change freeze. Halcyon Health does not.**

**Northwind Labs**
- **Holiday freeze: December 18, 2026 to January 4, 2027.** Only standard and emergency changes ship during this window [2].
- **Month-end billing freeze:** no normal changes to Ledger from the last business day of the month until invoices are sent, usually the 2nd [2]. Since this recurs monthly, it likely applies around December 31, though the policy doesn't name that date [2].
- Rollbacks are allowed at any time, freeze or not [2][5].
- Normal changes need sign-off from the owning team's change approver, and the VP Engineering can approve if the approver and delegate are both unavailable [2].
- Deploys are normally allowed Monday to Thursday, 09:00–16:00 Pacific. Friday deploys need approval from the on-call engineering manager [5].
- The week of December 22 falls inside the holiday freeze, so expect only standard and emergency changes that week [1].

**Halcyon Health**
- There is no IT change freeze over the holidays. A steering committee note says so directly [3].
- Clinic managers asked that pilot training for the Juniper project not land in the week of December 21 [3]. This is a request, not a freeze.
- Changes to clinical systems still need approval from the system steward, and significant changes also need CSCAB review [6][9].

rows.answer:
**Err high.** At both organizations, if you can't tell how serious something is, rate it at the higher level.

**Northwind Labs (incidents):**
- Whoever declares the incident picks the initial severity. When unsure, declare higher, because downgrading is cheap [3].
- The incident commander (IC) can raise or lower the severity at any time [3].
- Only the IC can make that change during the incident. The on-call runbook defines SEV-1 as data loss or a full ingest or pipeline outage for a cell, SEV-2 as a partial outage or degraded performance affecting many customers, and SEV-3 as a single-customer or non-critical issue [2].

**Halcyon Health (patient safety events):**
- The policy says "When unsure, report at the higher level." Quality & Patient Safety (QPS) reclassifies if needed [1].
- The levels run from 1 (sentinel event) to 4 (near miss) [1].
- The policy is owned by QPS and approved by the Patient Safety Committee [1]. The knowledge base doesn't say who else can change a rating, so QPS is the documented authority.

**Northwind's helpdesk vendor (Hollowpine Software Co.)** is held up by a disagreement over training data. Hollowpine's DPA draft arrived in July 2026, and redlines have been with legal since August. The main open point is Hollowpine's right to use ticket content to train its reply-suggestion model [2]. Until the DPA is signed, Hollowpine runs under security exception SEC-EX-117, approved by the Head of Security on August 24, 2026 [2]. The security review also requires AI reply suggestions to stay disabled until the DPA is signed [2]. The contract renews January 31, 2027 [2].

**Halcyon's patient survey vendor (Tallgrass Survey Co.)** is held up by data retention. The business associate agreement (BAA) draft arrived in August 2026. Tallgrass wants to keep identifiable survey responses for 5 years for benchmarking, while Halcyon will accept 18 months [10]. The Privacy Officer, Margaret Holloway, is due to send revised retention language by November 6, 2026 [10]. The security risk assessment is complete, having passed with conditions in September 2026, and the signed order form is on hold until the BAA is executed [10]. No PHI may be shared with Tallgrass until the BAA is signed, including for pilots [10]. If the BAA is not signed by January 31, 2027, Quality & Patient Safety will look at other survey vendors [10].

**Halcyon offers the bigger discount: 20% versus Northwind's 15%.** The two are not like-for-like, though, and the Halcyon discount has an important exclusion.

- **Northwind:** Annual prepayment on the Growth plan earns a 15% discount, equivalent to $12,240 per year [1]. The September 2026 sales desk memo confirms this 15% still applies under the new discount rules [2].
- **Halcyon:** Self-pay patients who pay in full on the day of service receive a 20% prompt-pay discount [3]. For example, the self-pay rates are $165 for a new patient visit, $120 for an established visit, and $79 for telehealth [3].
- **Exclusion:** The 20% does not apply to vaccines and injectables, which are already priced at cost plus administration [5]. Sliding-fee patients get their program discount instead [3][5].

The two discounts also apply to different things: Northwind's is a percentage off a software contract's first-year value, while Halcyon's is a percentage off a single self-pay visit. Neither source says whether the discounts can be combined with other offers.

rows.answer:
**Northwind Labs:** The incident commander (IC) can approve an emergency change, but only during a declared incident. The owning team's change approver then reviews it afterwards, within two business days [4][5]. You can find the approver for each team in the engineering team directory, and each team also has a named delegate [7]. The IC can approve even changes that would normally need the owning team's approver [5].

**Halcyon Health:** The on-call medical director may approve an emergency change, but only to stop ongoing patient harm [1]. The on-call medical director for the network is reached through the answering service at 555-0144, option 2 [2]. The change is then reviewed by the Clinical Systems Change Advisory Board (CSCAB) at its next weekly meeting, which is on Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern [1]. The policy doesn't set a separate deadline for that review. The November rota names the on-call director by week, and I didn't check who is on call this week [2].
